title: Question 1 (Page 9, #14)
question: Why is it important for root hair cells to have an elongated protrusion?
explanation: Students must be familiar with the structure-function of root hair cells.

options.option_text: to contain chlorophyll to produce glucose for the root cell
to drill through rocks in the soil to obtain more mineral salts
to increase more space for the central vacuole to store more water
to increase surface area to volume ratio for absorption of ions and water

title: Question 2 (Page 9, #15)
question:
Four different plant cells are shown in the diagram below. Which of these descriptions of all the features of the cells are correct?

&&img&& PAGE_9_Q15 &&img&&
explanation: Cell G is the xylem cell, which is a dead cell, thus it is a fully permeable cell with no nucleus or chloroplast.

options.option_text: E: partially permeable, nucleus absent, chloroplast present
F: partially permeable, nucleus present, chloroplast absent
G: fully permeable, nucleus absent, chloroplast absent
H: fully permeable, nucleus absent, chloroplast present

title: Question 3 (Page 9, #16)
question:
Two types of specialised cells, X and Y, are shown below. Where can these cells be found in the human body?

&&img&& PAGE_9_Q16 &&img&&
explanation: X shows a row of ciliated cells which line the trachea. These function to sweep mucus and dust particles towards the pharynx. Y shows a row of epithelial cells with microvilli, which line the small intestine to aid in more efficient absorption of digested molecules.

title: Question 4 (Page 9, #17)
question:
The diagram shows a type of cell isolated from an organism. What is its likely function in the organism?

&&img&& PAGE_9_Q17 &&img&&
explanation: The presence of microvilli to increase surface area suggests that it has a role in absorption.

title: Question 5 (Page 9, #18)
question:
A student saw an image of a cell under a microscope as shown below. Which of the following statements explain why the cell above is not a plant cell?

&&img&& PAGE_9_Q18 &&img&&
explanation: A typical plant cell has a cell wall and one or two large central vacuoles that an animal cell does not possess. Some plant cells also have chloroplasts which are not present in typical animal cells.

title: Question 6 (Page 9, #19)
question: What is the structure and function of organelle Z?
explanation: Mitochondria can be characterised as oval shaped organelles with membrane folds. They are essential for their role in releasing energy from aerobic respiration.

options.option_text: mitochondrion: site of respiration to release energy
ribosome: transports substances around the cell

title: Question 1 (Page 10, #20)
question:
Name organelles W, X and Y.

&&img&& PAGE_10_Q20 &&img&&
explanation: W is the nucleus, a large, often spherical organelle that contains genetic material. X is the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, characterised by a network of smooth, flattened layers that are connected together. Y is the Golgi apparatus, which is characterised by flattened layers that are not connected to each other.

options.option_text: W: nucleus, X: Golgi apparatus, Y: smooth endoplasmic reticulum
W: nucleus, X: smooth endoplasmic reticulum, Y: Golgi apparatus
W: nucleus, X: rough endoplasmic reticulum, Y: Golgi apparatus
W: nucleus, X: ribosome, Y: smooth endoplasmic reticulum

title: Question 2 (Page 10, #21)
question: Which organelles will be involved in the production of α-haemoglobin protein found in red blood cells?
explanation: Since α-haemoglobin is a protein produced in the cell, the genetic information in the haemoglobin gene of the nucleus (W) is needed to produce mRNA, which will then be translated into polypeptide chain by the ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum (V). The polypeptide is then repackaged into functional proteins (proteins which have biological activities) by the Golgi apparatus (Y).

title: Question 3 (Page 10, #22)
question:
The diagram shows a three-dimensional model of an animal cell. X and Y are organelles that perform important functions in the cell. What will the tissues faced by the cell be if organelles X and Y are absent?

&&img&& PAGE_10_Q22 &&img&&
explanation: Organelle X is the mitochondrion, which releases energy needed for active transport. Organelle Y is the nucleus, which contains genetic information needed for cell repair and division.

options.option_text: organelle X absent: no active transport, organelle Y absent: cannot repair damaged cell
organelle X absent: cannot produce proteins, organelle Y absent: no active transport
organelle X absent: cannot repair damaged cell, organelle Y absent: cannot transport substances
organelle X absent: cannot synthesise fats, organelle Y absent: cannot undergo cell division

title: Question 4 (Page 10, #23)
question:
The diagrams show different groups of cells found in the human body. What do these groups of cells represent?

&&img&& PAGE_10_Q23 &&img&&
explanation: All the diagrams show similar cells grouped together to form tissues that carry out a specific function.

options.option_text: organelles that carry out different functions
organs that carry out different functions
systems that carry out specific life processes
tissues that carry out a specific function

title: Question 5 (Page 10, #24)
question:
The diagram shows the different organelles found in a cell. Which of these statements about the cell is true?

&&img&& PAGE_10_Q24 &&img&&
explanation: This cell is a plant cell as evidenced from the presence of the cell wall. It contains chloroplasts; thus this should be from the green stem instead of the root or xylem.

options.option_text: This cell is found in the green stem as it contains chloroplasts.
This cell is found in the liver of an animal as it contains many mitochondria.
This cell is found in the root of a plant as it contains more than one central vacuole.
This cell is found in the xylem as there are perforations in the cell wall.

title: Question 1 (Page 11, #25)
question:
The diagram shows a plant cell. Along which plane was the three-dimensional plant cell sliced in order to obtain the two-dimensional view of the plant cell as shown above?

&&img&& PAGE_11_Q25 &&img&&
explanation: Plane D is the only plane that cut across the nucleus of the three-dimensional cell. Since the nucleus is visible in the two-dimensional cell, it must be cut at plane D.

title: Question 2 (Page 11, #26)
question:
A student made the following observations about two different cells, R and S, viewed under an electron microscope. What will the likely identities of cells R and S be?

&&img&& PAGE_11_Q26 &&img&&
explanation: All descriptions of cell B hint that it is a plant cell. The presence of an elongated extension shows that it is likely to be the root hair cell. Cell S is an animal cell due to lack of cell wall and large central vacuole. Only the nerve cell has numerous extensions branching out in all directions.

options.option_text: cell R: cabbage root hair cell, cell S: human nerve cell
cell R: cat red blood cell, cell S: tomato leaf cell
cell R: human nerve cell, cell S: cabbage root hair cell
cell R: tomato leaf cell, cell S: cat red blood cell

title: Question 3 (Page 11, #27)
question:
The diagram shows a cell from the lining of the intestine. Which of the following statements correctly describes the cell?

&&img&& PAGE_11_Q27 &&img&&
explanation: The numerous extensions, known as microvilli (singular: microvillus) play an essential role in absorbing digested food by increasing surface area to volume ratio.

options.option_text: The cell has a cell wall to prevent mechanical damage caused by the flow of undigested food.
The cell has a nucleus to control substances moving in and out of the cell.
The cell has multiple folds to increase surface area to volume ratio for efficient absorption.
The cell has numerous mitochondria to provide energy for diffusion to take place.

title: Question 4 (Page 11, #28)
question:
The diagram shows a photomicrograph of a drop of blood. Based on the diagram above, which correctly identifies the structural adaptation of the red blood cell that allows it to perform its function?

&&img&& PAGE_11_Q28 &&img&&
explanation: From the diagram, the only adaptation that can be observed is the circular shape of the red blood cell. The clear hollow-like appearance in the middle of the circular cell, B and C, although factually correct, cannot be observed from the diagram.

options.option_text: Circular biconcave shape increases surface area for efficient gaseous exchange.
Contains large amounts of haemoglobin to transport oxygen to the rest of the body.
Flexible, allowing the red blood cell to squeeze through narrow capillaries.
Secretes enzymes that promotes blood clotting to repair damage in the blood vessel.

title: Question 1 (Page 12, #29)
question: When a blue stain was added to a sample containing both living and dead plant cells, only the dead cells were stained blue. Which structure is most likely preventing the stain from entering the living cells?
explanation: The cell membrane forms a partially permeable layer that prevents some substances from entering the cell freely. Since the cell membrane was most likely damaged when the cell died, the blue stain would be able to enter the dead cell.

title: Question 2 (Page 12, #30)
question: Which of the following parts of a plant are complex tissues?
explanation: Simple tissues are made up of similar cells which work together to perform a specific function. Complex tissues contain different cell types performing a specific function. The lower leaf epidermis consists of epidermal and guard cells while the phloem consists of sieve tube elements and companion cells, so these two tissues are complex tissues.

title: Question 3 (Page 12, #31)
question:
The diagram shows the Escherichia coli (E. coli) bacterium. Which of the following features can be found in both the E. coli as well as a typical plant cell?

&&img&& PAGE_12_Q31 &&img&&
explanation: The diagram shows that the E. coli has a cell wall.

title: Question 4 (Page 12, #32)
question:
Cells store energy released by aerobic respiration in the mitochondria in the form of adenosine triphosphate (ATP). The energy stored in ATP is often used for metabolic activities. The table shows three unknown cells and the average number of mitochondria present in the cells. What will the likely identity of cells 1, 2 and 3 be?

&&img&& PAGE_12_Q32 &&img&&
explanation: The red blood cell lacks a nucleus and most of its organelles including mitochondria to free space for more haemoglobin. The heart muscle cell contracts regularly and requires a large number of mitochondria for energy. The stem contains an average number of mitochondria.

options.option_text: cell 1: heart muscle cell, cell 2: xylem cell, cell 3: liver cell
cell 1: liver cell, cell 2: skin cell, cell 3: red blood cell
cell 1: red blood cell, cell 2: heart muscle cell, cell 3: skin cell
cell 1: skin cell, cell 2: xylem cell, cell 3: heart muscle cell

title: Question 5 (Page 12, #33)
question: In a scientific investigation, amoeba cells, whose nuclear membrane was damaged slightly, were placed in a solution containing radioactively-tagged amino acids required for the repair of the nuclear membrane. Some amoeba cells were then removed at regular intervals and analysed for the sites of radioactivity. Which of the following shows the sequence at which radioactivity first appeared in the organelles?
explanation: The radioactive amino acids are subunits to produce radioactively-tagged proteins that can be used for the repair of the nuclear membrane. The ribosomes on the rough endoplasmic reticulum will be the first to come into contact with the amino acids to synthesise proteins, which will be processed by the Golgi apparatus before being transported to the nuclear membrane for repair.

options.option_text: Golgi apparatus → rough endoplasmic reticulum → nuclear membrane
Golgi apparatus → smooth endoplasmic reticulum → nuclear membrane
rough endoplasmic reticulum → Golgi apparatus → nuclear membrane
smooth endoplasmic reticulum → Golgi apparatus → nuclear membrane

title: Question 1 (Page 13, #34)
question:
HMG-coA reductase is an enzyme that catalyses the formation of cholesterol. Which organelles are directly responsible for the production of HMG-coA reductase and cholesterol respectively?

&&img&& PAGE_13_Q34 &&img&&
explanation: HMG-coA reductase is a protein that is manufactured in the ribosomes of the rough endoplasmic reticulum (U), while cholesterol is a steroid that is manufactured in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (J).

title: Question 2 (Page 13, #35)
question:
The Euglena is classified as a separate kingdom called the Protista as it has certain features that make it unsuitable to be categorised as a plant or an animal. Which of the following features justifies why Euglena cannot be classified as a plant or an animal?

&&img&& PAGE_13_Q35 &&img&&
explanation: Plant cells are immobile, thus having a flagellum that enables mobility to the cell makes Euglena not suitable to be categorised as a plant. Animal cells on the other hand have no chloroplasts to make food, and hence, Euglena cannot be considered as an animal cell too.

options.option_text: cannot be classified as a plant: has a flagellum, cannot be classified as an animal: has chloroplasts
cannot be classified as a plant: has chloroplasts, cannot be classified as an animal: has flagellum
cannot be classified as a plant: has no cell wall, cannot be classified as an animal: has a nucleus
cannot be classified as a plant: has contractile vacuole, cannot be classified as an animal: has cell membrane

title: Question 3 (Page 13, #36)
question: The contractile vacuole of the Euglena expels excess water that is absorbed into the cell due to the high water potential of the freshwater surroundings. This is essential for the survival of Euglena. Cells of submerged freshwater plants on the other hand have no need for contractile vacuoles to ensure their own survival. Which of the following best explains why freshwater plant cells do not need the contractile vacuoles to ensure their own survival?
explanation: The cellulose cell wall plays a major role in preventing plant cells from undergoing lysis due to excessive water gain. Having a large central vacuole to store water will still result in the lysis of the cell if the cell membrane is stretched beyond its limits.

options.option_text: The plant cells have a cell membrane that is less permeable to water as compared to the Euglena, thus less water will be absorbed.
The plant cells have a large central vacuole that can store excess water and preventing the plant cells from bursting.
The plant cells have more mitochondria that enable the cells to expel excess water via active transport.
The plant cells have rigid cell walls that prevent the cell from bursting due to excessive water absorption.

title: Question 4 (Page 13, #37)
question:
One major difference between a Euglena cell and a typical plant cell is that the Euglena cell has a flagellum that confers it mobility. Which of these organelles will the Euglena cell have in abundance as compared to a typical plant cell?

&&img&& PAGE_13_Q37 &&img&&
explanation: The flagellum requires large amounts of energy to propel the cell forward, thus more mitochondria is needed for releasing the required energy via aerobic respiration.

title: Question 5 (Page 13, #38)
question:
The diagram refers to some cellular structures. Which area in the diagram represents human red blood cells and a root hair cell?

&&img&& PAGE_13_Q38 &&img&&
explanation: Red blood cells do not have a nucleus so are incapable of cell division. Since centrioles have a role in cell division, they would be absent in red blood cells. Red hair cells would not have centrioles as centrioles are only found in animal cells.

options.option_text: red blood cell: 1, root hair cell: 2
red blood cell: 5, root hair cell: 9
red blood cell: 5, root hair cell: 4
red blood cell: 6, root hair cell: 7

title: Question 1 (Page 14, #1)
question:
The diagram shows a plant cell. Identify which labelled structures allow for osmosis to occur.

&&img&& PAGE_14_Q1 &&img&&
explanation: Osmosis can only occur through partially permeable membranes. In this case, only the cell membrane (1), the nuclear membrane (2) and the tonoplast (4) are partially permeable, hence allow for osmosis to occur across them.

title: Question 2 (Page 14, #2)
question:
The diagram shows three different processes whereby molecules move in organisms. Which of the following identifies the processes correctly?

&&img&& PAGE_14_Q2 &&img&&
explanation: Process X shows diffusion—the movement of solute molecules from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration. Diffusion does not require the presence of a partially permeable membrane, but it can occur in the presence of one. Process Y shows osmosis—the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential across a partially permeable membrane. Process Z shows active transport—the movement of molecules from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration, with the expenditure of energy.

options.option_text: process X: active transport, process Y: osmosis, process Z: diffusion
process X: diffusion, process Y: osmosis, process Z: active transport
process X: diffusion, process Y: active transport, process Z: osmosis
process X: osmosis, process Y: diffusion, process Z: active transport

title: Question 3 (Page 14, #3)
question: Which of these processes require energy from the oxidation of glucose?
explanation: Energy is needed to move molecules against a concentration gradient (from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration). Process Z, which is the active transport, is the only process where molecules move against a concentration gradient. Processes X and Y, which are diffusion and osmosis respectively, involve the movement of molecules down a concentration gradient, so energy is not required.

title: Question 4 (Page 14, #4)
question: Which of the following comparisons between diffusion and osmosis is not correct?
explanation: Both diffusion and osmosis involve the movement of molecules down a concentration gradient. For osmosis specifically, water molecules move down a water potential gradient.

options.option_text: diffusion: does not require a partially permeable membrane, osmosis: requires a partially permeable membrane
diffusion: down a concentration gradient, osmosis: against a concentration gradient
diffusion: occurs in gases and liquids, osmosis: occurs in solutions
diffusion: involves all types of molecules except water molecules, osmosis: involves water molecules only

title: Question 5 (Page 14, #5)
question: Which of these processes require energy from respiration?
explanation: Active transport is the only process which requires energy that is released by the mitochondria during cellular respiration. Diffusion and osmosis are both passive processes, meaning that they do not require energy in order to occur.

options.option_text: diffusion: requires energy, osmosis: requires energy, active transport: does not require energy
diffusion: requires energy, osmosis: does not require energy, active transport: does not require energy
diffusion: does not require energy, osmosis: requires energy, active transport: requires energy
diffusion: does not require energy, osmosis: does not require energy, active transport: requires energy

title: Question 6 (Page 14, #6)
question: Some processes which occur in plants and animals are listed. Which of these processes require energy?
explanation: Uptake of ions by root hair cells and uptake of glucose by intestinal villi occur via active transport, so they require energy from cellular respiration. Movement of oxygen from the alveoli into capillaries is via diffusion, so does not require energy. The movement of water up the xylem vessels is mainly via transpiration pull, which also does not require energy.

title: Question 1 (Page 15, #7)
question: Which of the following processes requires the presence of a partially permeable membrane?
explanation: Absorption of water by root hair cells is via osmosis which occurs across the cell membrane of the root hair cells. Evaporation (B), transpiration pull (C) and transpiration (D) do not require the presence of a partially permeable membrane.

options.option_text: absorption of water by root hair cells
evaporation of water into mesophyll intercellular air space
movement of water up the stem
movement of water vapour out through the stomata

title: Question 2 (Page 15, #8)
question: Which of these processes can take place in a root hair cell in the absence of oxygen?
explanation: In the absence of oxygen, aerobic respiration cannot occur so energy cannot be released. Active transport requires energy from cellular respiration so it cannot occur in the absence of oxygen.

title: Question 3 (Page 15, #9)
question: Which of these liquids has the lowest concentration of solutes?
explanation: Distilled water consists of only water molecules with no other solutes. The rest of the options are solutions consisting of different solutes dissolved in water.

title: Question 4 (Page 15, #10)
question:
A plant cell is immersed in a concentrated sugar solution and its appearance after 30 minutes is shown below. What is found in the region labelled X?

&&img&& PAGE_15_Q10 &&img&&
explanation: The cell wall is fully permeable so the sugar solution diffuses into the space between the cell wall and the cell membrane of the plasmolysed plant cell.

title: Question 5 (Page 15, #11)
question: Which of the following processes involves osmosis?
explanation: Osmosis involves movement of water molecules through a partially permeable membrane, thus option B is the answer. Options C and D depict movement of water without the presence of a membrane. Option A does not involve the movement of water, thus will not be considered osmosis.

options.option_text: Absorption of glucose in the ileum
Absorption of water in the colon
Flowing of water down a slope
Transport of water up the xylem

title: Question 6 (Page 15, #12)
question:
The diagram shows a U-shaped tube containing two solutions that are separated by a partially permeable membrane. In which direction will most water molecules move in relation to their concentration gradient?

&&img&& PAGE_15_Q12 &&img&&
explanation: The 5% sugar solution has a higher water potential than the 10% sugar solution. Water molecules move from the 5% sugar solution to the 10% sugar solution across the partially permeable membrane by osmosis.

options.option_text: from left arm to right arm against their concentration gradient
from left arm to right arm down their concentration gradient
from right arm to left arm against their concentration gradient
from right arm to left arm down their concentration gradient

title: Question 7 (Page 15, #13)
question:
The graph shows the effect of oxygen concentration in blood on the uptake of glucose molecules in the intestinal villi. What conclusion can be made based on the graph?

&&img&& PAGE_15_Q13 &&img&&
explanation: The rate of glucose uptake is affected proportionally by oxygen concentration. This is evidence that increased cellular respiration gives rise to increased glucose uptake.

options.option_text: Glucose molecules enter the villi at low oxygen concentrations.
Glucose molecules leave the villi at low oxygen concentrations.
Glucose molecules enter the villi by active transport.
Glucose molecules leave the villi by active transport.

title: Question 1 (Page 16, #14)
question: A novice gardener added fertiliser solution that was twice the recommended concentration to his plants by mistake. He then realised that his plants appeared wilted after 24 hours despite providing the usual amount of water. Which of the following best explains his observation?
explanation: Wilting can be caused by the excessive loss of water vapour via the stomata, by the lack of water absorbed by the roots or due to the loss of water from the plant cells to the soil. Since the concentration of fertiliser was doubled, it is likely that the water potential in the soil was lower than the water potential in the cells of the plant, leading to osmosis of water molecules from the plant cells to the soil.

options.option_text: The high concentration of fertiliser inhibited active transport of water into the roots of the plants.
The plants were poisoned by the high concentration of fertilisers.
The water potential of the soil was lower than the water potential in the plant cell due to presence of the fertiliser.
The xylem vessels of the plants were blocked due to high concentration of nitrate ions in the soil, causing less water to be transported to the leaves.

title: Question 2 (Page 16, #15)
question:
The diagram shows a potometer being used to investigate the rate of water loss by a potato cylinder. Which of the following will be observed when the set-up is placed under sunlight for three hours?

&&img&& PAGE_16_Q15 &&img&&
explanation: The potato will lose water to the surroundings after being exposed to sunlight for a few hours. This results in water being absorbed by the potato via osmosis, reducing the volume of water in the potometer and causing the air bubble to move to the left. The water level of the water in contact with the potato will not decrease as it is replenished by the water in the capillary tube to the left of the air bubble.

options.option_text: The air bubble will move to the left towards the potato.
The air bubble will move to the right away from the potato.
The potato cylinder will shrink and fall into the potometer.
The water level of the distilled water in contact with the potato will decrease.

title: Question 3 (Page 16, #16)
question:
Four agar blocks of different sizes were fully submerged and suspended in a beaker containing red dye solution. Which agar block will take the longest time to be completely stained red?

&&img&& PAGE_16_Q16 &&img&&
explanation: The rate at which the block is completely stained depends on the surface area to volume ratio of the block. The smaller the surface area to volume, the slower it takes for the dye to diffuse into the agar block. Using the formula surface area to volume = total surface area/ total volume, B has the smallest surface area to volume ratio of 0.5, thus takes the longest time to be completely stained red.

title: Question 4 (Page 16, #17)
question:
A visking tubing is filled with 5% sugar solution and immersed in a boiling tube containing 15% sugar solution as shown in the diagram below. Which of the following correctly explains the observation after 30 minutes?

&&img&& PAGE_16_Q17 &&img&&
explanation: The 5% sugar solution has a higher water potential than the 15% sugar solution. Water molecules will move from the 5% sugar solution into the 15% sugar solution across the partially permeable visking tubing by osmosis, causing the contents in the visking tubing to decrease in mass.

options.option_text: Sugar molecules have moved from the 15% sugar solution into the visking tubing by osmosis, hence the visking tubing increases in mass.
Sugar molecules have moved out of the visking tubing into the 15% sugar solution by osmosis, hence the visking tubing decreases in mass.
Water molecules have moved from the 15% sugar solution into the visking tubing by osmosis, hence the visking tubing increases in mass.
Water molecules have moved out of the visking tubing into the 15% sugar solution by osmosis, hence the visking tubing decreases in mass.

title: Question 5 (Page 16, #18)
question:
Some cells were extracted from a green plant. Half of the cells were immersed in solution A and the other half was immersed in solution B. The appearance of the cells after 30 minutes is shown below. What could solution A and solution B be?

&&img&& PAGE_16_Q18 &&img&&
explanation: The cell in solution A appears firm and turgid, suggesting that it has been placed in a hypotonic solution, and water molecules have entered the cell via osmosis. The cell in solution B appears plasmolysed, suggesting that it has been placed in a hypertonic solution of very high concentration, and water molecules have left the cell via osmosis.

options.option_text: Solution A: 30% sugar solution, Solution B: water
Solution A: 5% sugar solution, Solution B: water
Solution A: 5% sugar solution, Solution B: 5% sugar solution
Solution A: water, Solution B: 30% sugar solution

title: Question 1 (Page 17, #19)
question:
The diagram shows some body cells bathed in tissue fluid. Under which conditions would water molecules enter the body cells?

&&img&& PAGE_17_Q19 &&img&&
explanation: Tissue fluid with a low solute concentration would have a relatively high water potential. Since osmosis involves the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential, water molecules would enter the cell from a tissue fluid of low concentration to the cells if they have a low water potential.

options.option_text: concentration of tissue fluid: high, water potential of cytoplasm of body cells: high
concentration of tissue fluid: high, water potential of cytoplasm of body cells: low
concentration of tissue fluid: low, water potential of cytoplasm of body cells: high
concentration of tissue fluid: low, water potential of cytoplasm of body cells: low

title: Question 2 (Page 17, #20)
question:
An investigation was conducted to find out the effect of increasing salt solution on the change in length of potato strips. The results are plotted in the graph below. What is the concentration of the salt solution that is isotonic to the cell sap of the potato cells?

&&img&& PAGE_17_Q20 &&img&&
explanation: When the concentration of salt solution is isotonic (same) to the cell sap, there will not be any change in the length of the potato strips. When the value of initial length/final length = 1, the concentration of salt solution is 0.4 M.

title: Question 3 (Page 17, #21)
question:
The diagram shows part of a plant with three cells labelled 1, 2 and 3. The arrows show the movement of water molecules by osmosis. Which is the correct order of water potential in the cells from the highest to the lowest?

&&img&& PAGE_17_Q21 &&img&&
explanation: In cell 2, water molecules only move out, suggesting that it has the highest water potential. In cell 3, water molecules only move in, suggesting that it has the lowest water potential.

title: Question 4 (Page 17, #22)
question: After digestion, glucose molecules are absorbed from the lumen of small intestine into the blood capillaries to be carried towards the liver. Which of the following conditions correctly identifies how glucose is absorbed into the blood?
explanation: After a meal, there is a high concentration of glucose molecules in the intestinal lumen, so they are absorbed into the blood stream mainly by diffusion, down a concentration gradient. Before a meal, there is a low concentration of glucose molecules in the intestinal lumen, so they are absorbed into the blood stream mainly by active transport, against a concentration gradient.

options.option_text: before/after meal: after, process: active transport, movement: down concentration gradient
before/after meal: after, process: diffusion, movement: against concentration gradient
before/after meal: before, process: active transport, movement: against concentration gradient
before/after meal: before, process: diffusion, movement: down concentration gradient

title: Question 5 (Page 17, #23)
question:
Four solutions of different concentrations, P, Q, R and S, are set up as shown below. The set-up is then left aside for two hours. Rank the solutions from the lowest concentration to the highest concentration.

&&img&& PAGE_17_Q23 &&img&&
explanation: The solution with the lowest concentration will have the highest water potential so the most amount of water molecules will leave the funnel through the visking tubing via osmosis. It will thus have the lowest water level after two hours. Conversely, the solution with the highest concentration will have the lowest water potential so the most amount of water molecules will enter the funnel through the visking tubing via osmosis. This funnel will then have the highest water level after two hours.

title: Question 1 (Page 18, #24)
question: A dialysis tubing was filled with a salt solution, starch solution, protein solution, and some saliva. It is then immersed into a beaker of water. What would you expect to find inside the beaker of water after one hour?
explanation: The dialysis tubing is partially permeable so only small molecules can pass through. Amylases in saliva are able to digest starch to become maltose molecules which are small. So after an hour, salt and maltose, which are small, will be able to diffuse from inside the dialysis tubing to the water in the beaker. Proteins, including amylase, are too large to pass through the partially permeable dialysis tubing, hence remain inside the tubing.

title: Question 2 (Page 18, #25)
question: A fresh potato cube is placed into a test-tube containing a sucrose solution of unknown concentration. After a while, its mass increased. What process has occurred and what is the concentration of the sucrose solution?
explanation: In order for the potato cube to gain mass, water molecules must have moved into it via osmosis. Thus the potato cells have a lower water potential than the sucrose solution.

title: Question 3 (Page 18, #26)
question:
A plant cell was placed in a sugar solution of unknown concentration. After 20 minutes, the plant cell appears as shown below. What caused the change and what type of solution was the plant cell placed in?

&&img&& PAGE_18_Q26 &&img&&
explanation: The plant cell is in a plasmolysed state—a phenomenon where the cell has shrunk to the extent such that the cell membrane detaches from the cell wall. This happens when the cell loses too much water via osmosis.

options.option_text: Sugar moved into the cell, dilute
Sugar moved out of the cell, concentrated
Water moved out of the cell, concentrated

title: Question 4 (Page 18, #27)
question:
The graph shows how the rate of uptake of ions may be affected by oxygen concentration. Which lines indicate the rate of ion uptake by diffusion and active transport?

&&img&& PAGE_18_Q27 &&img&&
explanation: The rate of diffusion is not affected by oxygen concentration at all so the graph for diffusion should remain constant at all oxygen concentrations. Active transport requires energy from cellular respiration to occur so its rate increases as oxygen concentration increases.

title: Question 5 (Page 18, #28)
question:
The diagram shows two adjacent leaf cells, X and Y. Cell X has a higher water potential than cell Y. Which cell is closer to the xylem and in which direction does the water move between these cells?

&&img&& PAGE_18_Q28 &&img&&
explanation: Osmosis of water molecules can only take place from a region of higher water potential (X) to a region of lower water potential (Y). Since these cells are in the leaf, the direction of water flow is from the xylem to the leaf cell. This means that cell X should be closer to the xylem to allow water to move via osmosis from the xylem to X and eventually to Y.

options.option_text: X (nearer xylem), from X to Y (direction of water movement)
X (nearer xylem), from Y to X (direction of water movement)
Y (nearer xylem), from X to Y (direction of water movement)
Y (nearer xylem), from Y to X (direction of water movement)

title: Question 1 (Page 19, #29)
question:
Some carrot tissues were immersed in varying concentrations of sugar solutions for 30 minutes. The results of the experiment are as shown below. From the graph, deduce which sugar solution is isotonic to the carrot cells.

&&img&& PAGE_19_Q29 &&img&&
explanation: When the carrot cells were immersed in an isotonic solution, the water potential of the cells and the solution were the same, thus there would be no net change in length of the carrot tissue. From the graph, there is no change in length when the concentration of sugar solution was 0.2 mol dm-3.

title: Question 2 (Page 19, #30)
question:
Four fresh onion rings are cut and their diameters are measured before being placed into sucrose solutions of different concentrations. After an hour, the onion rings are removed from the solutions and their diameters are measured again. The table shows the measurements. Which solution, P, Q, R or S, had the lowest sucrose concentration?

&&img&& PAGE_19_Q30 &&img&&
explanation: The onion ring placed in solution R showed the greatest increase in diameter. This means that water molecules had entered the onion ring via osmosis, thus the solution itself had the highest water potential compared to the cells in the onion rings.

title: Question 3 (Page 19, #31)
question:
Four beakers with dialysis tubings are set up. Each beaker and dialysis tubing contains a different solution as shown below. In which set-up, will the dialysis tubing appear the most firm after 30 minutes?

&&img&& PAGE_19_Q31 &&img&&
explanation: The solutions in beakers A and C have a higher water potential than the solutions inside the respective dialysis tubings. This causes an influx of water molecules into the dialysis tubings by osmosis, causing the tubings to appear firm. The concentration gradient in beaker C is steeper than that of beaker A, hence the dialysis tubing in C will become firmer than that in A. Whereas, the solutions in beakers B and D have a lower water potential than the solutions inside the respective dialysis tubings. Water molecules will move out of the dialysis tubings by osmosis, and hence, the tubings will have reduced mass and become less firm.

options.option_text: 5% sugar solution outside, 15% sugar solution inside
15% sugar solution outside, 5% sugar solution inside
5% sugar solution outside, 25% sugar solution inside
25% sugar solution outside, 5% sugar solution inside

title: Question 4 (Page 19, #32)
question:
The diagram shows a leaf section. Identify the arrows which represent the movement of substances by diffusion during photosynthesis.

&&img&& PAGE_19_Q32 &&img&&
explanation: During photosynthesis, the palisade mesophyll cells require carbon dioxide and water. However, only the carbon dioxide enters the leaf and subsequently the palisade cells by diffusion. The water enters the cells from the xylem via osmosis. The oxygen produced diffuses out of the intercellular air spaces as there is a lower concentration of oxygen in the atmospheric air.

title: Question 5 (Page 19, #33)
question:
A root hair cell and a red blood cell are both placed in a dish of 30% sucrose solution. Which row correctly describes these cells after one hour?

&&img&& PAGE_19_Q33 &&img&&
explanation: The vacuole of the root hair cell and cytoplasm of the red blood cell both have a higher water potential than the 30% sucrose solution. Water molecules will move from these cells into the sucrose solution. This will cause the root hair cell to become plasmolysed and the red blood cell to become crenated.

options.option_text: root hair cell: crenated, red blood cell: crenated
root hair cell: flaccid, red blood cell: flaccid
root hair cell: plasmolysed, red blood cell: crenated
root hair cell: turgid, red blood cell: flaccid

An experiment is set up as shown in the diagram below to investigate the movement of water molecules. Which combination of solutions P and Q will cause the visking tubing to show the greatest gain in mass after 10 minutes?

&&img&& PAGE_20_Q34 &&img&&
explanation: In order for the visking tubing to gain mass, water molecules must move into the visking tubing by osmosis. Hence, solution Q needs to be of a higher water potential than solution P. In both options R and C, solution Q has a higher water potential than solution P. However, since the concentration gradient is higher in option B, the visking tubing will show the greatest gain in mass.

solution P: 10% starch solution, solution Q: distilled water
solution P: 15% starch solution, solution Q: 10% starch solution
solution P: distilled water, solution Q: 5% starch solution

title: Question 2 (Page 20, #35)
question:
Penguins can be found in many coastal areas in the southern hemisphere. The diagram shows two different penguin species—the emperor penguin and the little blue penguin. The emperor penguin inhabits the coast of Antarctica, with an average annual temperature of -10°C. The little blue penguin can be found in New Zealand, where the average annual temperature is around 10°C. Which statement best explains why emperor penguins are found in Antarctica while little blue penguins are found in New Zealand?

&&img&& PAGE_20_Q35 &&img&&
explanation: As the average temperature in Antarctica is much lower than in New Zealand, the emperor penguins must be adapted to lose heat at a much slower rate than the little blue penguins. Since emperor penguins are larger in size, they have a smaller surface area to volume ratio as compared to the little blue penguins, thus losing heat less readily.

options.option_text: Emperor penguins have a larger surface area to volume ratio, thus lose heat less readily.
Emperor penguins have a larger surface area to volume ratio, thus lose heat more readily.
Emperor penguins have a smaller surface area to volume ratio, thus lose heat less readily.
Emperor penguins have a smaller surface area to volume ratio, thus lose heat more readily.

title: Question 3 (Page 20, #36)
question:
The diagram shows the movement of substances from atmospheric air to the air spaces in the leaf, and between the air spaces in the leaf and the cells of the leaf. Which arrow(s) show(s) the diffusion of gases during photosynthesis?

&&img&& PAGE_20_Q36 &&img&&
explanation: During photosynthesis, carbon dioxide from atmospheric air diffuses into the leaves through the stomata (arrow 4) and into photosynthesising cells (arrow 2). At the same time, oxygen produced diffuses out of the cells and into the intercellular air spaces (arrow 3) before they subsequently diffuse out through the stomata.

title: Question 4 (Page 20, #37)
question: Based on the extract: 'Chromosomes are not able to move across the nuclear membrane to carry genetic information directly to the ribosomes in the endoplasmic reticulum. Messenger RNA are molecules which carry partial genetic information from the chromosomes to the ribosomes for them to carry out protein synthesis.' Which of the following conclusions can be made?
explanation: Messenger RNA molecules are smaller than chromosomes and are thus able to traverse across the partially permeable nuclear membrane. They then pass this genetic information to the ribosomes which are then involved in the synthesis of proteins from RNA. This question requires students to integrate information from these chapters—Cells, Movement of Substances and Molecular Genetics.

title: Question 5 (Page 20, #38)
question: Which of the following organelles can diffuse into and out of the nucleus?
explanation: Nucleotides are the smallest subunits of DNA and RNA molecules. Genes are found on chromosomes and do exist independent of chromosomes, so even though they are small, they are not able to diffuse across the partially permeable nuclear membrane.

title: Question 1 (Page 21, #39)
question:
Four strips of equal length and mass are cut from a fresh cucumber then placed into solutions of varying sugar concentration. After an hour, the appearance of the strips taken from the different solutions is shown below. From the results obtained, arrange the solutions in increasing order of sugar concentration.

&&img&& PAGE_21_Q39 &&img&&
explanation: The cucumber skin has a layer of wax that will reduce the movement of water molecules into the cucumber via the skin. However, the other side of the cucumber has no skin and will allow water molecules to enter or exit via osmosis. The solution with the lowest concentration will have the highest water potential and water molecules will move from the solution into the cucumber strip causing the highest upward curvature (strip C). The strip with the highest concentration will have the lowest water potential; water molecules will move from the cucumber strip into the solution causing the downward curvature (4).

title: Question 2 (Page 21, #40)
question: Which of the following cell types are likely to have an abundance of mitochondria?
explanation: Cells with an abundance of mitochondria usually have high energy demand for cellular activities. The intestinal epithelial cell and the root hair cell have a high energy requirement as they are involved in active transport. The sperm cell requires energy, not for active transport, but to enable the sperm to swim. The red blood cell and xylem cell do not have a high energy requirement so they will have a normal distribution of mitochondria.

title: Question 3 (Page 21, #41)
question:
The graph shows the uptake of potassium ions in the roots of a maize plant in the presence and absence of oxygen. Which of the following statements best describes how the roots of the maize plant takes in potassium ions?

&&img&& PAGE_21_Q41 &&img&&
explanation: Active transport is dependent on the presence of oxygen as it requires energy released from aerobic respiration to transport ions against the concentration gradient. Diffusion, on the other hand, is a passive process that can happen in the absence of oxygen and aerobic respiration. From the graph, there is still intake of substantial amounts of potassium ions in the absence of oxygen, thus only diffusion is involved in the transportation of ions into the roots. The curve showing uptake of potassium ions in the presence of oxygen suggests that diffusion occurs initially when the concentration of potassium ions was higher in the soil as compared to the root cells. However, as the concentration of potassium ions in the soil becomes equal or lower than that in the root cell, active transport takes over to pump ions into the root cell against the concentration gradient. The amount of potassium ions taken in by active transport can be estimated by the difference in levels of ions transported between the two curves. Since the amount of potassium ions taken in by diffusion and active transport are about the same, option D is not true.

options.option_text: The roots take in potassium ions by active transport only.
The roots take in potassium ions by diffusion only.
The roots take in potassium ions by both active transport and diffusion.
The roots take in more potassium ions by active transport than by diffusion.

title: Question 4 (Page 21, #42)
question:
Three experimental set-ups were prepared to investigate the effects of different salt concentrations on the rate of osmosis in potato cells. A depression is made on each potato cube and filled with salt solutions with different concentrations. Which of the following shows the likely results after 12 hours?

&&img&& PAGE_21_Q42 &&img&&
explanation: In set-up 1, the water potential of the concentrated solution in the tray was lower than that of the potato cells and the dilute salt solution, thus water molecules moved via osmosis from the dilute salt solution, through the potato cells into the tray causing the water level in the depression to decrease slightly while the water level in the tray increased slightly. In set-up 2, water molecules moved via osmosis from the distilled water in tray into the concentrated solution in the depression causing the water level in the depression to increase while the water level in the tray decreased. In set-up 3, the rate of osmosis of water from the distilled water in the tray into the dilute solution in the depression was slower as the water potential gradient was smaller compared to set-up 2, thus water levels in the tray decreased slightly while water level of depression increased slightly.

options.option_text: Set-up 1: water level risen, Set-up 2: water level risen, Set-up 3: water level risen
Set-up 1: water level unchanged, Set-up 2: water level unchanged, Set-up 3: water level unchanged
Set-up 1: water level unchanged, Set-up 2: water level unchanged, Set-up 3: water level lowered
Set-up 1: water level lowered, Set-up 2: water level unchanged, Set-up 3: water level risen

title: Question 1 (Page 22, #43)
question:
The graph shows the difference in concentration of sodium, Na+ ions inside a cell and in the fluid surrounding the cell. Which of the following conclusions can be made from the graph above?

&&img&& PAGE_22_Q43 &&img&&
explanation: From the graph, the concentration of the ions are higher in the cell than outside the cell, suggesting that sodium ions are transported into the cells via active transport, and thus energy is required. Since ions are able to move into the cell, the cell membrane must be partially permeable. Since the concentration of the sodium ions decreases as the distance from the cell membrane increases within the cytoplasm, it shows that movement of ions within the cytoplasm is from a region of high concentration to a region of lower concentration, thus must be via diffusion. Since the cell membrane is partially permeable, there will be some sodium ions that will leave the cell into the surrounding via diffusion.

in beaker purple, in visking tubing purple

question: Which of the following statements is not true about enzymes?

Enzymes speed up the rate of biological reactions.
Lipases catalyse the conversion of fats to fatty acids and glycerol.

Graph showing rate of enzyme activity increasing then leveling off with temperature
Graph showing rate of enzyme activity increasing then decreasing with temperature (bell curve)

question: Enzyme action is often explained by the 'lock-and-key' hypothesis. In this hypothesis, where is the active site, and which is the lock and key?
explanation: In the 'lock-and-key' hypothesis, the enzyme is the lock while the substrate is the key. The active site is located on the enzyme and has a complementary shape to that of the substrate.

options.option_text: active site: on the enzyme, key: enzyme, lock: substrate
active site: on the enzyme, key: substrate, lock: enzyme
active site: on the substrate, key: enzyme, lock: substrate
active site: on the substrate, key: substrate, lock: enzyme

title: Question 1 (Page 32, #13)
question: Which of the following can cause the active site of an enzyme to change its shape?
explanation: The change in the three dimensional shape of an enzyme's active site is due to exposure to high temperatures and is known as denaturation.

options.option_text: The enzyme has been cooled to 10°C.
The enzyme has been heated to 60°C.
The enzyme has been immersed in a concentrated sugar solution.
The enzyme has been immersed in a dilute sugar solution.

title: Question 2 (Page 32, #14)

&&img&& PAGE_32_Q14 &&img&&

options.option_text: Graph showing enzyme activity peaking early and plateauing at low temperatures
Graph showing enzyme activity plateauing at higher temperatures
Graph showing enzyme activity with bell curve peaking around 40-50°C

&&img&& PAGE_32_Q15 &&img&&
explanation: Students are again advised to read the labels of the axes carefully before making sense of the graph. Graph showing substrate amount decreasing then increasing

explanation: The most common mistake committed by students is the choice of graph C. Students need to read the labels of the axes carefully before interpreting the graph. options.option_text: Graph showing products amount increasing then plateauing
Graph showing products amount increasing then decreasing
Graph showing products amount with bell curve pattern
Graph showing products amount increasing linearly

title: Question 5 (Page 32, #17)
question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are true of all enzymes?
explanation: All enzymes lower the activation energy of biochemical reactions as they provide an alternative pathway of lower activation energy for the reaction to occur. Enzymes catalyse many reactions in organisms and their effects are not limited only to the digestive system. Enzymes, being catalysts, remain unchanged at the end of every reaction. Since enzymes catalyse many reactions in all organisms, they can also be found in plants.

title: Question 6 (Page 32, #18)
question: Which of the following are properties of enzymes found in blood?
explanation: Enzymes are highly specific in their action and can only react with one type of substrate. They are affected by temperature and pH, but not carbon dioxide concentration. Since hydrogen ion concentration affects pH, the enzymes will also be affected by hydrogen ion concentrations. As enzymes are chemically unaltered by the reactions they catalyse, they can be reused multiple times, hence only a small amount of enzymes is needed to catalyse any chemical reaction.

title: Question 1 (Page 33, #19)
question:
Potato cells produce catalase enzyme which is able to convert toxic hydrogen peroxide into harmless oxygen and water. An experiment was carried out to investigate the conditions affecting catalase activity in potato cells soaked in hydrogen peroxide solution. Four set-ups, A, B, C and D, were prepared with differences in the number and condition of potato discs used. In which experimental set-up would there be the most oxygen collected?

&&img&& PAGE_33_Q19 &&img&&
explanation: The higher the number of potato discs, the higher the amount of catalase present, which would lead to a faster rate of decomposition of hydrogen peroxide to release oxygen. Boiling of the potato disc would lead to denaturation of catalase, thus not being able to catalyse the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. As such, option D with 10 raw potato discs would result in the highest amount of oxygen collected.

title: Question 2 (Page 33, #20)
question:
Taq polymerase is a heat stable enzyme that is extracted from a bacterium that thrives in hot springs and hydrothermal vents. This enzyme is used routinely in DNA amplification reactions in molecular laboratories. Which line correctly shows the activity of Taq polymerase after 40°C?

&&img&& PAGE_33_Q20 &&img&&
explanation: This enzyme has an optimum temperature that is way above 40°C since it is found in bacteria that is able to survive in temperatures beyond 60°C. Hence, above 40°C, the enzyme's rate of reaction would likely be increasing and not decreasing as depicted by options A, B and C.

title: Question 3 (Page 33, #21)
question: The enzyme tyrosinase catalyses the production of melanin via oxidation, causing the browning of potatoes that are exposed to air. Which of the following could be used to show that tyrosinase is an enzyme?
explanation: The high temperatures in the boiling water bath will denature tyrosinase if it is an enzyme, preventing any further browning of the potato. The procedures in options C and D prevent oxygen from coming into contact with the potato. Although this prevents the reaction from occurring due to absence of a substrate, it does not prove that tyrosinase is an enzyme. Sunlight has no effect on tyrosinase activity in the potato, thus option A will not prove that tyrosinase is an enzyme.

options.option_text: Leave the potatoes under direct sunlight and see if it turns brown.
Place the potatoes into a boiling water bath to see if it turns brown.
Place the potatoes into a sealed vacuum pack and see if it turns brown.
Soak the potatoes in salt water to see if it turns brown.

explanation: The enzyme is the 'lock' and the substrate is the 'key'. In this case, the enzyme and substrate are DNA polymerase and deoxyribonucleotides respectively.

title: Question 1 (Page 35, #30)

Graph B showing MnO₂ curve leveling off and catalase curve continuing to rise with temperature

title: Question 4 (Page 35, #33)
question: P and Q are reactants in an enzyme-catalysed reaction, whereby E is the enzyme. The product of this reaction is R. title: Question 1 (Page 36, #34)

title: Question 2 (Page 36, #35)
question: Two samples of salivary amylase were treated and used in an experiment to investigate the digestion of starch. title: Question 1 (Page 37, #1)

title: Question 3 (Page 37, #3)
question:
Which row correctly identifies the 'lock' and 'key' in the enzymatic digestion of starch?

&&img&& PAGE_37_Q3 &&img&&
explanation: In the 'lock-and-key hypothesis, the enzyme (amylase in this case) is the lock and the substrate (starch) is the key. Maltose is the digested product.

title: Question 4 (Page 37, #4)
question:

title: Question 5 (Page 37, #5)
question:
Which of the labelled parts are involved in the digestion of carbohydrates?

&&img&& PAGE_37_Q5 &&img&&

title: Question 6 (Page 37, #6)
question:

&&img&& PAGE_37_Q6 &&img&&

title: Question 7 (Page 37, #7)
question:
Which of the labelled part(s) do(es) not produce digestive enzymes?

&&img&& PAGE_37_Q7 &&img&&
explanation: The liver (1) produces bile which is stored and released by the gall bladder (2). Bile is not an enzyme as it does not catalyse a chemical reaction. The emulsification of fats is a physical process and not a chemical one, as the fats remain chemically unchanged during emulsification.

title: Question 8 (Page 37, #8)
question:

title: Question 9 (Page 37, #9)
question: What is the function of the gall bladder?

title: Question 10 (Page 37, #10)

explanation: Food moves down the oesophagus via peristalsis and not by gravity, hence the walls of the oesophagus are lined with muscles. Although no enzymes are produced in the oesophagus, the digestion of starch continues until the partially digested food reaches the stomach, where the acidic pH stops the action of the salivary amylase. No absorption of food occurs in the oesophagus; absorption of food starts only in the small intestine.

title: Question 1 (Page 38, #11)

The diagram shows a section in the alimentary canal where partially digested food is being pushed along. Which correctly describes the state of the circular and longitudinal muscles at 1 and 2?

&&img&& PAGE_38_Q11 &&img&&
explanation: The circular and longitudinal muscles work antagonistically. When the circular muscles contract at 2 to push the bolus of food leftwards, the longitudinal muscles will relax.

options.option_text: circular muscles 1: contracted, 2: relaxed; longitudinal muscles 1: contracted, 2: relaxed
circular muscles 1: contracted, 2: relaxed; longitudinal muscles 1: relaxed, 2: contracted
circular muscles 1: relaxed, 2: contracted; longitudinal muscles 1: contracted, 2: relaxed
circular muscles 1: relaxed, 2: contracted; longitudinal muscles 1: relaxed, 2: contracted

title: Question 2 (Page 38, #12)
question: Which of the following is not a function of the liver?
explanation: The liver produces bile, which is not a digestive enzyme. Bile emulsifies fats to increase the exposed surface area of fats for lipase action.

title: Question 3 (Page 38, #13)
question: Which of the following are functions of the liver? 1 production of bile 2 breakdown of haemoglobin 3 storage of excess amino acids 4 storage of excess glucose 5 breakdown of alcohol
explanation: The liver produces bile, breaks down haemoglobin, stores excess glucose in the form of glycogen and produces the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase which breaks down alcohol. Excess amino acids is not stored, instead are deaminated and converted to urea and glucose by the liver.

title: Question 4 (Page 38, #14)
question: Some alcohol can be broken down in the liver by the enzyme alcohol dehydrogenase. Excessive alcohol consumption, however, can have harmful effects on the body. Which of the following is not a short-term effect of excessive alcohol consumption?
explanation: Liver cirrhosis usually occurs with prolonged alcohol abuse and is a long-term effect of excessive alcohol consumption.

title: Question 5 (Page 38, #15)
question: Which of the following conversions does not take place in the liver?
explanation: Even though bile is produced by the liver, the emulsification of fats takes place in the small intestine and not the liver.

title: Question 6 (Page 38, #16)
question: Which row correctly associates the organ with its digestive function?
explanation: In the mouth, ingestion of food and partial digestion of starch occurs. In the liver, assimilation of glucose and amino acids takes place. In the small intestine, digestion of all food groups is completed and absorption of the digested food takes place.

options.option_text: mouth: digestion, liver: assimilation, small intestine: digestion
mouth: digestion, liver: absorption, small intestine: absorption
mouth: ingestion, liver: assimilation, small intestine: digestion
mouth: ingestion, liver: absorption, small intestine: absorption

title: Question 7 (Page 38, #17)
question: Which is the correct order of events during human nutrition?
explanation: Ingestion occurs in the mouth, followed by digestion. Absorption of fully digested food then takes place followed by assimilation, where the digested food absorbed is used for metabolic processes.

title: Question 8 (Page 38, #18)
question: The production of urea increases when a person's diet contains a large amount of
explanation: Proteins are digested to form the end products, amino acids. Excess amino acids in the body will be deaminated in the liver to form urea.

title: Question 9 (Page 38, #19)
question:
The diagram shows a transverse section of an intestinal villus. What are the structures X and Y?

&&img&& PAGE_38_Q19 &&img&&
explanation: X is the lacteal which transports away digested fats. Y is the intestinal cell where digested food molecules enter before moving into the blood capillaries or lacteals. The microvilli can be found on the surface of these intestinal cells.

title: Question 1 (Page 39, #20)
question:
The diagram shows an intestinal villus. What are the substances transported into vessels X and Y?

&&img&& PAGE_39_Q20 &&img&&
explanation: Fatty acids and glycerol recombine to form fat globules that are transported away by the lacteal. Amino acids and glucose are absorbed into the blood capillaries and transported to the hepatic portal vein.

options.option_text: vessel X: amino acids, vessel Y: glucose
vessel X: fatty acids, vessel Y: glycerol
vessel X: fat globules, vessel Y: amino acids
vessel X: glucose, vessel Y: amino acids

title: Question 2 (Page 39, #21)
question:
The diagram shows part of the small intestine's villus. Which of the labelled structures are responsible for absorption of digested fats and the secretion of digestive enzymes respectively?

&&img&& PAGE_39_Q21 &&img&&
explanation: Digested fats are absorbed into the lacteal (2) while gland cells (3) are responsible for the secretion of digestive enzymes.

options.option_text: absorption of digested fats: 1, secretion of digestive enzymes: 3
absorption of digested fats: 1, secretion of digestive enzymes: 4
absorption of digested fats: 2, secretion of digestive enzymes: 3
absorption of digested fats: 2, secretion of digestive enzymes: 4

title: Question 3 (Page 39, #22)
question:
Which labelled part is likely to contain cells with a high density of mitochondria?

&&img&& PAGE_39_Q22 &&img&&
explanation: Intestinal cells absorb glucose and amino acids both by diffusion and by active transport. Since active transport involves the uptake of glucose and amino acids against a concentration gradient, it requires energy from aerobic respiration. Hence, intestinal cells will have a high density of mitochondria in order to meet the energy demands of the cell for the absorption of glucose and amino acids.

title: Question 4 (Page 39, #23)
question: Which of the following substances does not produce a chemical conversion of nutrients?
explanation: Bile emulsifies fats into tiny fat globules, which increases the surface area to volume ratio for lipase to digest the fats. Emulsification does not change the chemical composition of fats.

title: Question 5 (Page 39, #24)
question: Which statement regarding the emulsification of fats is correct?
explanation: When fats are emulsified to fat globules, their surface area to volume ratio is increased significantly for lipase to digest them into fatty acids and glycerol.

options.option_text: It digests the fats into fatty acids and glycerol for absorption.
It enables the fat globules to be absorbed more quickly into the blood capillaries.
It enables the fat globules to be digested more efficiently.
It reduces the surface area of the fat molecules for reaction with lipase.

title: Question 6 (Page 39, #25)
question:
The diagram shows a type of movement in the alimentary canal that moves food X along the oesophagus. Which row identifies the movement and the food X?

&&img&& PAGE_39_Q25 &&img&&
explanation: In the oesophagus, partially digested food called the bolus, is pushed towards the stomach by peristalsis. Chyme is partially digested food that moves from the stomach towards the small intestine.

title: Question 7 (Page 39, #26)
question: Which row shows the incorrect pairing of the liver function with the corresponding chemical substance?
explanation: The liver deaminates amino acids to form urea but this urea is excreted in the kidneys and not the liver itself.

options.option_text: function: deamination, chemical substance: amino acids

title: Question 1 (Page 40, #27)
question:

&&img&& PAGE_40_Q27 &&img&&
explanation: Emulsification of lipids occurs in the ileum, the gall bladder merely secretes the bile needed into the small intestine via the bile duct.

options.option_text: breakdown of haemoglobin: liver, emulsification of lipids: gall bladder, churning of chyme: ileum, absorption of fatty acids: capillaries
breakdown of haemoglobin: liver, emulsification of lipids: ileum, churning of chyme: stomach, absorption of fatty acids: lacteal
breakdown of haemoglobin: spleen, emulsification of lipids: ileum, churning of chyme: duodenum, absorption of fatty acids: capillaries
breakdown of haemoglobin: spleen, emulsification of lipids: gall bladder, churning of chyme: stomach, absorption of fatty acids: lacteal

title: Question 2 (Page 40, #28)
question:
The graph shows the percentage of undigested substances as food passes through the alimentary canal. Identify organs X and Y.

&&img&& PAGE_40_Q28 &&img&&
explanation: In organ X, only protein digestion occurs so it is likely to be the stomach. In organ Y, proteins and fats are both digested, so it is likely to be the small intestine.

options.option_text: organ X: oesophagus, organ Y: stomach
organ X: stomach, organ Y: small intestine
organ X: stomach, organ Y: large intestine
organ X: small intestine, organ Y: large intestine

title: Question 3 (Page 40, #29)
question:
Which line represents the percentage of undigested starch as food passes from the mouth to the stomach and to the small intestine?

&&img&& PAGE_40_Q29 &&img&&
explanation: Amylases present in the mouth and small intestine will digest starch to maltose, causing the starch levels to decrease. There are no amylases present in the stomach, so starch levels will remain relatively constant in the stomach.

title: Question 4 (Page 40, #30)
question:
Which line represents cellulose fibres?

&&img&& PAGE_40_Q30 &&img&&
explanation: The human digestive system does not have the necessary enzymes (cellulases) to digest cellulose, unlike many herbivores. Since fibres are not digested in the human alimentary canal, their levels remain at 100% throughout.

title: Question 5 (Page 40, #31)
question:
Which bar chart represents the amount of protein digested in the mouth, stomach and small intestine of a human?

&&img&& PAGE_40_Q31 &&img&&
explanation: No proteases are present in the mouth, so no protein digestion occurs here. In the stomach, pepsin breaks down proteins to polypeptides. In the small intestine, proteins are broken down to polypeptides then to amino acids by trypsin and erepsin (peptidases) respectively.

options.option_text: Chart A showing amount of proteins digested in arbitrary units for mouth, stomach, and small intestine
Chart B showing amount of proteins digested in arbitrary units for mouth, stomach, and small intestine
Chart C showing amount of proteins digested in arbitrary units for mouth, stomach, and small intestine
Chart D showing amount of proteins digested in arbitrary units for mouth, stomach, and small intestine

title: Question 1 (Page 41, #32)
question:
Which labelled blood vessel will contain the highest concentration of nutrients after a heavy meal?

&&img&& PAGE_41_Q32 &&img&&
explanation: Blood rich in nutrients is transported first to the liver via the hepatic portal vein (vessel B) for assimilation before it is returned to the heart via the inferior vena cava (vessel C).

title: Question 2 (Page 41, #33)
question:
Which blood vessel is likely to show the greatest changes in composition throughout a typical 24-hour day?

&&img&& PAGE_41_Q33 &&img&&
explanation: Before meals, the hepatic portal vein will show a low concentration of glucose. After meals, the hepatic portal vein will show a high concentration of glucose. The other blood vessels will show a relatively constant level of glucose due to the homeostatic effect of insulin and glucagon.

title: Question 3 (Page 41, #34)
question:
After a meal, how is the blood affected by the liver as it passes between these blood vessels?

&&img&& PAGE_41_Q34 &&img&&
explanation: As blood passes from the hepatic artery (vessel 2) to the hepatic vein (vessel 1), amino acids and glucose are added to maintain a constant supply of nutrients in the blood for respiration and building of new protoplasm. These amino acids and glucose are brought to the liver from the small intestine via the hepatic portal vein (vessel 3).

options.option_text: blood vessels 2 to 1, effect of liver amino acids added
blood vessels 2 to 1, effect of liver urea removed
blood vessels 3 to 1, effect of liver amino acids added
blood vessels 3 to 1, effect of liver urea removed

title: Question 4 (Page 41, #35)
question: A piece of bread that is chewed in the mouth gradually tastes sweeter. What is the explanation for this phenomenon?
explanation: Saliva contains the enzyme amylase that converts starch to maltose. Maltose is a disaccharide sugar, hence it tastes sweet.

options.option_text: Saliva contains enzymes that break down starch in bread to glucose.
Saliva releases simple sugars from the bread.
Starch is converted to maltose by salivary enzymes.
The mouth secretes saliva that is sweet.

title: Question 5 (Page 41, #36)
question:
The table shows the chemical compositions of some foods. Which food(s) is/are likely to be digested in the stomach?

&&img&& PAGE_41_Q36 &&img&&
explanation: Proteins are digested in the stomach. Proteins contain the elements carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen.

title: Question 6 (Page 41, #37)
question:
The diagram shows the effect of pH on the activity of two enzymes, X and Y, in the alimentary canal. In which regions of the alimentary canal would these enzymes be found?

&&img&& PAGE_41_Q37 &&img&&
explanation: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and the enzymes there (eg. pepsin and rennin) function optimally at a low pH. The small intestine has an alkaline pH and enzymes active in the small intestine function optimally at a high pH.

options.option_text: X small intestine, Y large intestine

title: Question 7 (Page 41, #38)
question: The gall bladder of a man was surgically removed. Which of the activities below would he not be able to do?
explanation: Lipases produced by the pancreas and small intestine will allow him to still digest fats, but at a slower rate. His liver is also intact and will still be able to produce bile. Synthesis of fats is not a function of the gall bladder so will also not be affected.

title: Question 1 (Page 42, #39)
question: A type of birth deformation causes the inner lining of a baby's small intestine to be completely smooth. What is a likely consequence of this deformation?
explanation: A completely smooth inner lining of the small intestine will provide a much reduced surface area for absorption of digested nutrients. With reduced absorption of nutrients, the baby will become malnourished.

title: Question 2 (Page 42, #40)
question:
A person with a bacterial infection had part of his liver surgically excised. Which of the following are possible side effects from this surgery?
1 decreased production of amino acids
2 decreased urine concentration
3 reduced production of bile
4 slower fat digestion
explanation: The liver does not produce amino acids, so 1 is not true. The liver will have a reduced ability to convert excess amino acids to urea, resulting in a lower elimination in the urine. There will be less bile produced by the liver, hence, the digestion of fat becomes slower.

title: Question 3 (Page 42, #41)
question:
Three food samples, X, Y and Z, containing egg albumin, sucrose solution and olive oil respectively, were added into separate test tubes. Pancreatic juice was added into each sample which was then subjected to different conditions as shown in the table below.

Sample X: egg albumin + pancreatic juice, pH 8, temperature 25°C
Sample Y: sucrose solution + pancreatic juice, pH 7, temperature 37°C
Sample Z: olive oil + pancreatic juice, pH 2, temperature 70°C

After four hours, samples X, Y and Z were tested with biuret's test, Benedict's test and ethanol-emulsion test respectively. What would the expected result of the tests be?

&&img&& PAGE_42_Q41 &&img&&
explanation: The egg albumin in X would be digested into amino acids. However, the presence of enzymes in the pancreatic juice means that there would be a positive test (violet solution) for peptide bonds as enzymes are also proteins. Pancreatic juice does not contain sucrase and thus will not be able to digest sucrose into smaller reducing sugars. As sucrose is a non-reducing sugar, there will be a negative result for Benedict's test and the solution remains blue. Since the acidic and high temperature conditions would result in the denaturation of all enzymes, the olive oil remained undigested and would thus give a cloudy white emulsion for the ethanol-emulsion test.

options.option_text: biuret test on sample X: solution remains blue, Benedict's test on sample Y: brick-red precipitate formed, ethanol-emulsion test on sample Z: solution remains clear
biuret test on sample X: solution remains blue, Benedict's test on sample Y: solution remains blue, ethanol-emulsion test on sample Z: solution remains clear
biuret test on sample X: solution turns violet, Benedict's test on sample Y: brick-red precipitate formed, ethanol-emulsion test on sample Z: cloudy white emulsion
biuret test on sample X: solution turns violet, Benedict's test on sample Y: solution remains blue, ethanol-emulsion test on sample Z: cloudy white emulsion

title: Question 4 (Page 42, #42)
question:
The diagram shows four wells dug into a starch agar plate. Each well was filled with a different digestive secretion.

Well 1: saliva
Well 2: gastric juice
Well 3: pancreatic juice
Well 4: intestinal juice

After incubating for 1 hour at 35°C, the starch agar plate is inundated with iodine solution. Which of the following shows the correct corresponding colour for each well?

&&img&& PAGE_42_Q42 &&img&&
explanation: Saliva and pancreatic juice contain amylases which break down starch to form maltose. The absence of starch in these wells after 1 hour will cause the iodine to remain brown. Gastric juice and intestinal juice do not contain amylases which break down starch. The presence of starch in wells 2 and 4 after 1 hour will give a blue-black observation.

title: Question 5 (Page 42, #43)
question:
The table shows the rate at which two different nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine of a mammal. The rates are shown for a healthy intestine and an intestine that has been poisoned by a substance which stops cellular respiration.

Nutrient X: healthy intestine 30, poisoned intestine 29
Nutrient Y: healthy intestine 100, poisoned intestine 33

Based on the information, how do these two nutrients get absorbed in the small intestine?

&&img&& PAGE_42_Q43 &&img&&
explanation: Active transport requires energy released during aerobic respiration. The absorption rate of nutrient X shows no significant difference between a healthy and poisoned intestine, indicating that it is absorbed via diffusion. The absorption rate of nutrient Y shows a big difference between a healthy and poisoned intestine, indicating that much of nutrient Y is absorbed when respiration is not inhibited hence it is absorbed via active transport.

title: Question 1 (Page 43, #44)
question:
The table shows the results of a study into the absorption of digested nutrients in the presence and absence of oxygen. Based on this study, how many products are absorbed by active transport?

&&img&& PAGE_43_Q44 &&img&&
explanation: Active transport requires energy released during aerobic respiration. Aerobic respiration can only occur in the presence of oxygen. Amino acids and glucose absorption show a big difference in the presence and absence of oxygen, hence these two are absorbed by active transport.

mouth: green, stomach: blue, small intestine: red
mouth: blue, stomach: green, small intestine: red
mouth: red, stomach: blue, small intestine: green

explanation: Bile in test tube C first emulsifies the fats in oil, providing a larger surface area to volume ratio for the lipases to act. The lipases then digest the emulsified fats to fatty acids and glycerol. The fatty acids lower the pH in the mixture.

water - diffuses through stomata into intercellular air space

CO2 released peaks at midnight, CO2 taken in peaks at midday
Both CO2 released and taken in peak at midday
CO2 released peaks during day and night, CO2 taken in peaks at midday

title: Question 4 (Page 46, #9)
question:
Which of the following graphs correctly shows how temperature affects the rate of photosynthesis?

&&img&& PAGE_46_Q9 &&img&&
explanation: Photosynthesis reactions are catalysed by enzymes which are temperature sensitive. As temperature increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases, up to optimum temperature. As temperature increases beyond optimum temperature, rate of photosynthesis decreases rapidly as the enzymes are denatured.

title: Question 5 (Page 46, #10)
question:
Which of the following graphs correctly shows how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis?

&&img&& PAGE_46_Q10 &&img&&
explanation: As light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis also increases. As the rate of photosynthesis reaches a plateau beyond a certain point, light intensity is no longer the limiting factor for photosynthesis. Instead, increasing other factors like carbon dioxide concentration or temperature would increase the rate of photosynthesis. As light intensity does not affect enzyme activity, curve D is not the correct answer.

title: Question 6 (Page 46, #11)
question:
Under which of the following conditions will a plant show the greatest rate of photosynthesis?

&&img&& PAGE_46_Q11 &&img&&

light intensity 20 / lux, carbon dioxide concentration 0.4 / %, temperature 60 / °C

question:
